INDEPENDENT SIGNING / DEPLOYMENT ELIGIBILITY PACKET — monitor_review, 2026-10-25

Scope and boundary
This is a bounded read-only check of official Apple documentation and Apple Staff guidance current at this assessment. No developer-account access, certificate request, private-key export/use, signing, download/install, build, kext load, USB/audio/MIDI client, service or security change was performed. No new narrative report was written. The following is eligibility evidence for .17, not an admitted kernel backend or permission to change SIP/startup policy.

1. Native architecture is separate from signing
Apple requires Apple Silicon kexts to contain arm64e, including pointer authentication and kernel restrictions. The current user-space arm64 HAL/MIDI artifacts are therefore not evidence that a reconstructed kernel executable is ABI-correct, linked, or loadable. This requirement does not prove that the entire original audio implementation must become a user HAL. Source: Apple, Implementing drivers, system extensions, and kexts, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/implementing-drivers-system-extensions-and-kexts .

2. Normal signed deployment: special certificate, not an ordinary app identity
Apple's current notarization documentation explicitly permits kext distribution using a Developer ID Application certificate with the kext capability. The corresponding Apple-issued leaf certificate has both Developer ID Application OID 1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13 and kext OID 1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.18. Ordinary Developer ID Application has .13 without the required kext extension; Developer ID Installer (.14) is for packages, not the kext executable. The published Developer ID CPS v3.2 (June 2, 2021), section 4.11.3, specifies both .13/.18 as mandatory critical certificate extensions plus code-signing EKU 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3. This older published profile is corroborated by current Apple Staff guidance below; no claim is made that v3.2 is the latest CPS. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/resolving-common-notarization-issues ; https://images.apple.com/certificateauthority/pdf/Apple_Developer_ID_CPS_v3.2.pdf .

The kext authorization is in an Apple-issued certificate. A locally added entitlements plist or provisioning profile cannot manufacture that CA-issued extension. Apple Development uses a distinct WWDR trust path; its acceptance by MIDIServer for this project's plug-in does not establish kext capability. TN3127 identifies ordinary Developer ID's issuer OID .100.6.2.6 and Apple Development's WWDR issuer .100.6.2.1. OID inspection is meaningful only with the Apple certificate chain; an arbitrary issuer could copy the same OID. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3127-inside-code-signing-requirements .

3. Current Apple Staff confirmation, with eligibility limits
In July 2026, Apple DTS confirmed that an ordinary Developer ID Application certificate remains insufficient for kext notarization. DTS says kext signing approval historically went to corporate, not individual/personal, accounts and that new requests are unlikely to be approved. That is current first-party guidance about the approval path, not a determination of this user's account type, existing permissions, or the outcome of a future application. No account was inspected and no approval request is authorized. A previously issued ordinary certificate does not become kext-enabled merely because a later account approval exists: the signing leaf must actually include .18. Sources: Apple Staff replies in https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391 and the linked Apple DTS certificate-inspection guidance https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/52353 .

4. Signed deployment versus temporary personal testing
For normally distributable kexts, DTS specifies a kext-enabled Developer ID signature plus notarization and the required reduced startup security. Apple's installation documentation separately requires Apple Silicon user consent, third-party-kext allowance, auxiliary kext-collection rebuild and reboot. Reduced Security is not a substitute for a missing kext-capable certificate or notarization. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391 ; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/installing-a-custom-kernel-extension .

The same July 2026 DTS reply explicitly distinguishes personal development: its stated current Apple Silicon path is SIP disabled plus Permissive Security in recoveryOS, rather than notarizing a personal product with an ordinary app certificate. Apple's September 17, 2026 deployment guide describes Reduced and Permissive as different policies and says SIP must be off before enabling Permissive. This is a materially different testing condition, not an approved normal-deployment result or evidence that this user accepts it. No policy-modification commands are proposed or executed here. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391 ; https://support.apple.com/en-ca/guide/deployment/dep5810e849c/web . Apple limits SIP disabling to necessary temporary development and directs reenabling after testing: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/disabling-and-enabling-system-integrity-protection .

5. Entitlements/profiles and notarization are different checks
A kext-enabled signing certificate is not the same thing as a DriverKit managed entitlement/profile. Apple documents DriverKit's entitlement and provisioning-profile authorization separately; those mechanisms must not be imported into the kernel candidate merely because both are called drivers. Generic macOS code needs a provisioning profile when it claims restricted entitlements; this pass found no evidence that a generic Mac/DriverKit profile replaces kext certificate authorization. It does not assert that every conceivable companion client needs no profile: any actual restricted client entitlement must be audited separately. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/pcidriverkit/creating-custom-pcie-drivers-for-thunderbolt-devices ; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3125-inside-code-signing-provisioning-profiles .

For distribution, Apple's notary prerequisites exclude Apple Development, ad hoc and local-development certificates; valid signatures and secure timestamps are required. Its Hardened Runtime rule is explicitly for app and command-line targets, so do not blindly treat a user-space runtime/entitlement recipe as a kext requirement. Notarization or a clean generic codesign verification alone is not a kernel-load proof. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution ; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3161-inside-code-signing-certificates .

6. What local metadata can and cannot establish
Public signing metadata can establish the certificate class, issuer/Apple trust chain, validity interval and kext OID presence. Apple DTS's documented inspection extracts only public certificates from signed code; it does not require exporting a private key. A read-only identity listing additionally identifies locally available identity references, but no signing attempt was made to test key usability. Certificate metadata cannot determine unqueried account eligibility, permissions absent from a cached certificate, future Apple approval, installed AuxKC admission, actual startup policy, binary ABI correctness or hardware operation. No private names/team identifiers are necessary in the evidence packet.

# Kernel binding admission: policy and signing gate

Research date: **2026-10-25 UTC**. Authority: **rigkontrol3-40h.17** in Beads.
Scope: one bounded, read-only primary-source pass before coding or security
changes. This note supplements [the parity audit](ParityAudit.md); it does not
close `.17` or select deployment preferences for the user.

**The original kernel audio model exists on this ARM Mac, but a usable loading
path for a newly reconstructed kext is not established under the present
constraints. Reduced Security alone is insufficient for personal kext development
without an approved kext-signing identity, and does not itself establish a deprecated-KPI exception. No fallback
architecture is automatically selected.**

## Availability and admission are separate

The completed static audit found real arm64e IOAudioFamily code in this Mac's
boot collection and defined matches for 184 of 186 original audio-family
imports. Retaining IOAudioDevice/IOAudioEngine while replacing legacy USB with
kernel IOUSBHostFamily remains the smallest structural candidate identified;
that is not a loading, signing or stability guarantee. Exact hashes and
comparison limits remain in the parity audit and `.13`.

Apple classifies legacy **IOUSBFamily as unsupported since macOS 11**, whereas
**IOAudioFamily is deprecated since 12.3**. Its published policy says deprecated
KPI kexts do not load by default; its footnote exempts SIP-disabled or
MDM-approved kexts from deprecation-policy enforcement. Thus the deprecated
category is neither an ARM availability proof nor an unrestricted admission
promise. Applying that published default to this new IOAudioFamily driver is
a policy inference, not an observed macOS 27.0.1 load attempt.
[Apple deprecated-kext policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

The same page's USB vendor-specific IPC restriction is conditional on the
driver not tying into an IOFamily subsystem. The original audio driver does
tie into IOAudioFamily. That prevents automatically treating it as a standalone
USB IPC case, but does not establish approval for a newly reconstructed driver.
[Apple USB policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

## Four independent gates

| Gate | What the primary evidence establishes | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native API/ABI | Original kernel code needs arm64e/PAC and a replacement for legacy USB. | That an x86 binary, old vtable layout or decompiler casts can be transplanted. |
| Deprecated-KPI policy | Default enforcement and the published SIP/MDM exceptions are separate from API presence. | That ordinary manual approval or Reduced Security alone overrides deprecation policy. |
| Signing and distribution | A suitable kext-enabled signing identity and the relevant distribution checks are distinct requirements. | That an Apple Development or ordinary Developer ID identity is sufficient. |
| Startup/user authorization | Apple Silicon kext installation uses explicit authorization, an auxiliary collection and a restart. | Consent to alter this Mac's security or proof that its present startup policy permits the candidate. |

Apple requires arm64e for Apple Silicon kexts and limits kernel extensions
where an equivalent system-extension solution exists. These are constraints
on the candidate, not proof that this particular NI implementation has an
approved equivalent or that a particular replacement is the minimum change.
[Apple implementation guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/implementing-drivers-system-extensions-and-kexts)

## Security modes and policy exceptions

For ordinary signed third-party kext installation, Apple documents enabling
kexts through recoveryOS, Reduced Security, authorization and an AuxKC rebuild
and restart. With SIP enabled, signatures are checked before inclusion; with
SIP disabled, that signature check is not enforced. An authorized list can
still contain kexts excluded from the resulting collection.
[Apple kernel-extension security](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/security/sec8e454101b/web)

**Reduced Security and SIP disabled are different conditions.** Apple's
current startup-policy guide distinguishes Full, Reduced and Permissive
Security. The personal-development route must not be described as
ordinary Reduced Security. An MDM exception to deprecation policy likewise
does not manufacture a valid signing identity, working native code or user
consent. No MDM enrollment/profile is being proposed or applied here.
[Apple startup security, published 2026-09-17](https://support.apple.com/en-ca/guide/deployment/dep5810e849c/web)

## Signing: distributable and personal paths

Apple's signing guidance identifies a kext-enabled Developer ID Application
certificate by its kext extension OID **1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.18**, in addition
to the Developer ID Application extension **1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13**.
Ordinary app signing is not equivalent. This older DTS reference is corroborated by the July 2026
staff answer below; no account request or certificate operation occurred.
[Apple DTS signing reference](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/52353),
[Apple Developer ID certificate profile, v3.2 §4.11.3](https://images.apple.com/certificateauthority/pdf/Apple_Developer_ID_CPS_v3.2.pdf).
The profile is a published historical certificate specification, corroborated
by the current staff guidance; it is not presented as the latest CPS.

Apple's notarization documentation requires new or updated kexts to be
notarized for its distributable path and specifies the appropriate Developer
ID certificate types. Notarization is not a replacement for the right signing
identity or for startup/loading approval.
[Apple notarization requirements](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution),
[Apple kext certificate diagnostics](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/resolving-common-notarization-issues)

In **July 2026**, Apple DTS CoreOS/Hardware engineer Kevin Elliott addressed
personal-use Apple Silicon kexts directly: the testing path requires SIP
disabled and Permissive Security. He reported that kext-signing approval had
been limited to corporate accounts and new requests were unlikely. Quinn
separately distinguished distributable signing/notarization from personal
testing. These are current, attributable staff statements, not a guarantee
about this user's account or future decisions. Only the Apple staff replies,
not the questioner's reported experiment, support this conclusion.
[Apple DTS personal-use clarification](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391)

## Technical minimum and remaining contract gates

The installed **macOS27.0 Kernel.framework headers**, compared against the
pinned original NI2.8.0 mappings, can represent the ring and calendar model.
This is a static source/API finding, not a compile, load or stability result.
Full header hashes, line ranges and original method addresses are in the

`IOUSBHostPipe.h` documents the legacy migration and absolute-frame ISO I/O;
`IOUSBHostInterface.h` promises controller-compatible non-bounced allocation.
The API accepts a suitable IOMemoryDescriptor; `createIOBuffer` is the

Those declarations do not guarantee NI's primary-interrupt publication cadence

The audio family retains timestamp, sample-position, pause/resume and stream
client roles. The USB family also imposes a per-port workloop. Their composition,

user-client contracts are representable, but actual access and compatibility
remain unverified. No FIFO, new queue lead, new clock algorithm or new private
transport is forced by these inspected kernel APIs.

The selected SDK contains the relevant audio/modern USB headers; legacy USB
headers are absent. Xcode/clang metadata supports AArch64. No local KDK was
found, but that observation alone proves neither a universal KDK requirement
nor inability to build. No compiler/linker test or toolchain installation was

user-process plug-ins use their documented native ABI.

**Minimum structural-change candidate:** retain reconstructed
`IOAudioDevice`/`IOAudioEngine`, its sample-positioned ring, workloop and
lifecycle, replacing the USB binding with **kernel IOUSBHostFamily** and the
required source/ABI changes. This is an engineering inference from the inspected
contracts, not a validated or policy-approved deployment recommendation.

caller-owned lists/storage, and `clearStall(bool withRequest)`; that Boolean
choice is closer to NI's calls than the current user API.

**Not justified as unavoidable:** replacing the kernel audio model with the
current AudioServerPlugIn, default pthread/dispatch handoff, new inter-bundle

may require a deployment rationale, but “ARM has no IOAudioEngine” is false on
this inspected Mac. A user-API limitation does not prove that selecting that
API was necessary.

**Unresolved deployment gate:** a new driver using deprecated IOAudioFamily
must satisfy current loading policy, suitable signing authorization and the
user's security constraints. General Apple Silicon kext installation involves
approval, auxiliary collection rebuilding/restart and Reduced Security settings;
Reduced Security alone does not prove this specific deprecated-family driver
will be admitted. The audit did not inspect/change startup security, request
signing authorization, install a KDK or compile/load a kext. The absence of a
local KDK is a tooling observation, not an impossibility proof.
[Apple custom-kext installation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/installing-a-custom-kernel-extension),
[Apple deployment requirements](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/deployment/depa5fb8376f/web)

**Disposition:** the bounded necessity assessment stops here. Beads **`.17`**
requires one explicit minimum-change deployment/binding decision before coding
or timing work. It must use the actual constraints above. It cannot silently
continue the current HAL, start another backend, reduce security or select

title: Preserve NI completion order across the modern USB callback binding
description: A production-ISO fake-host reproduction with whole-IRP primary publication and only1ms delay on slot0 exposes an introduced ready-FIFO/consumed-epoch dependency cycle when tied callbacks arrive slot1 before slot0. At bus5198 FIFO=[1,0], read_cursor0 alreadyconsumed; slot0 requeue needed to advance cursor sits behind blocked slot1. After128ms all64 inputs stall with no panic. Same delay with calendar-order delivery runs20s. Original NI readHandler directly scans then requeues; it has no new epoch/FIFO wait. Restore the original implicit per-pipe ordered completion contract in the current USB binding, preserving NI ring/calendar and buffer lifetime. This deterministic deadlock is not yet linked to the separate live TooOld fault (.11).

Every delivery checks the transfer still has the event's saved scheduled frame, preventing a reentrant new submission from receiving an obsolete event. GREEN changes only that tied-delivery ordering to forward slot order, so slot0 retires first. title: Verify HAL output activity and sleep lifecycle against original NI behavior
description: The faithful ARM port maps NI last-output-client inactive clear to output StreamIsActive, and expects modern host StopIO/StartIO across sleep to restore NI enterSleep/awakeFromSleep wire-clear and clock-anchor/timer behavior. Neither binding equivalence is physically demonstrated. Original wake unsuspends the USB device, queries its status and resets audio timing; it does not explicitly rearm EP1. Do not invent a wake-triggered EP1 retry. Validate the actual host lifecycle on the installed faithful build and change only a demonstrated missing binding.
acceptance_criteria: With a normal CoreAudio client, observe output StreamIsActive when the last output client stops while input continues; verify original literal inactive clear and no old audio replay on restart. Sleep/wake with audio and persistent MIDI active must restore correct wire/clock behavior and responsive controls, with no phantom switch actions or unexplained generation churn. If host I/O continues across sleep without the original reset, identify the documented current power binding and implement the minimum evidence-derived equivalent. Record logs and physical results; mock success alone is insufficient.

Severity correction: the earlier review observation that command_suspended can remain set after NotResponding is a real current state-machine property, but it is NOT established as a divergence from NI. No explicit original wake-driven EP1 read rearm was found. Do not invent a blanket power-notification retry or describe one as recovered NI behavior.

Original NIUSBAudioDevice::performPowerStateChange at0x1fe0 calls the base IOAudioDevice implementation first. On transition from state0 to state1 or2, instructions0x2023..0x2039 invoke provider-device virtual slot+0x988 with false, then+0x950 with a two-byte local status pointer. Anchoring the known GetVendorID/GetProductID slots0x8f0/0x8f8 against Apple's published IOUSBDevice virtual declaration order resolves these to SuspendDevice(false), then GetDeviceStatus(USBStatus*). The override then calls initialized engine awakeFromSleep0xbcb0. A transition to state0 calls engine enterSleep0xbc50. The provider calls are not command-IN read submissions.

Original enterSleep0xbc50 cancels the timestamp timer at engine+0xbd98 and zeros USB/host anchor and prior-measurement fields+0xbd70/+0xbd78/+0xbd80/+0xbd88. Original awakeFromSleep0xbcb0 resets refresh counter+0xbd90 and scaled interval+0xbd58 to10000000000, calls clearSampleBufferForStream0x7510 for the output groups, updates USB-cycle timing, establishes a fresh anchor and rearms timestamp maintenance at128ms while the device remains initialized/present. It has no direct EP1 read/rearm call.

A search across all241 private original C-like exports for the command-IN pipe member+0x920 and its Read virtual slot+0x1d0 found submissions in initHardware0x0db0 and the ordinary commandReplyDispatch0x20e0 tail. No additional direct NI wake submission was found. commandReplyDispatch's NotResponding branch aborts command IN and OUT and returns without entering the rearm tail; Aborted also returns. Current NativeUSB deliberately mirrors that no-rearm branch. This source search does not prove every indirect base/provider behavior, and does not prove that normal sleep necessarily triggers NotResponding.

The current IOUSBHost binding caches physical service termination and ignores nontermination interest messages. It has no dedicated original enterSleep/awakeFromSleep lifetime/anchor invalidation path if existing IO remains active. A real host StopIO/StartIO sequence resets/drains ISO/rings/anchors and may be the necessary modern sleep binding, but that substitution is physically UNVERIFIED. If the host does not stop/restart IO, explicit original wake wire-clear and clock-reset behavior is not currently mapped. Preserve this as a power-binding validation/compatibility question. Do not equate a powered-on notification with permission to replay commands, reset USB generation or rearm a suspended EP1 reader.

title: Complete original NI ring, clock and host-semantics parity
description: The same-backing output ring, exact mode-2/G1 positions/carry/wrap, original queue calendar, whole-batch denominator and zero-event formulas are implemented with tests. Remaining parity gaps include modern primary-interrupt publication proof, current host activity/power equivalence, and a confirmed anchor-maintenance cadence difference (NI interval update128ms, anchor every8ticks versus current probe each128ms). Shared memory representation does not establish timing equivalence. Audit .13 now gates implementation; no blanket claim that all clocks or architecture substitutions match.
acceptance_criteria: Original output descriptor/CPU-ring identity, sample-frame placement, wrap, capture polling, priming and timestamp relationships are reconstructed with instruction evidence. Current ARM/macOS memory/DMA ownership guarantees are resolved. A minimal platform mapping and explicit parity/deviation table exist before implementation. No arbitrary queue-lead workaround is presented as a faithful port. Temporal/continuity tests model real deadlines and the actual shared-ring contract.
notes:
ORIGINAL NI AUDIO EVIDENCE — 2026-10-25

Governing scope
Decision .5 records the user's explicit ARM lift-and-shift constraint. This issue is to reconstruct the original semantics faithfully and resolve binding compatibility, not invent a replacement audio architecture. Code/build/installation/experimentation stopped while .4 captures the checkpoint.

Provenance and evidence quality
Input NIUSBAudioDriver 2.8.0 (R36), x86_64 kernel extension, SHA-256 41574699c507896cb3a51b4756143e8c445eb76994871eb13517a642f7adaf08. Active-worktree private original: .build/ni/reference/2.8.0/NIUSBAudioDriver.x86_64. Private exports: .build/ni/decompiled/audio280-text/. Ghidra 12.2 completed 241 original functions in __text [0x710,0xe0fc). Important relationships below were checked in instruction exports, not only guessed pseudocode types. Addresses are original image-relative addresses; some recovered method prototypes omit/mistype this and indirect virtual calls need reconstruction.
Do not redistribute the full proprietary C-like exports/binary in source or Beads. The following is a behavioral account and provenance map. Committed report: ReverseEngineering/AudioDriver.md. Export/reproduction tools: Tools/DecompileDriver.java and Tools/decompile-drivers.sh. The newly discovered shared-ring relationship was found after cc1afd9; older reports may not state its full significance yet.

1. Same backing ring is used by USB descriptors and host sample writes — established
prepareMemory at 0x59d0 prepares the output descriptor stored at engine +0xb928. It obtains that descriptor's CPU view through virtual slot +0x2e0 and stores the pointer at engine +0xb930. Instructions around 0x5a5b..0x5a6b establish this descriptor-to-pointer identity. These are not two independent copies.
allocIsocIrps at 0x70e0 initializes output IRP descriptors referencing that storage.
queueOutIrp at 0x7620 constructs segments from descriptor +0xb928 at ring cursor +0xb988. Segment lengths follow accepted input microframe counts. Transfers crossing the end split into end-of-ring and beginning-of-ring descriptor segments.
clipOutputSamples at 0x6ab0 receives host firstSampleFrame and frame count, converts host float output to packed wire representation and writes directly through pointer +0xb930. Assembly from about 0x6bb4 explicitly accesses that pointer. Placement is based on host sample-frame position, channel grouping and wire width.
Conclusion supported by instructions: NI's host-facing PCM writes update the same backing storage referenced by preposted USB descriptors. It is not a FIFO snapshot taken at each queue call.
Private export basenames include 000059d0_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__prepareMemory.{c,asm}, 000070e0_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__allocIsocIrps.c, 00007620_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__queueOutIrp.c, and 00006ab0_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__clipOutputSamples.{c,asm}.

2. Queue calendar — established, but not a physical latency measurement
performAudioEngineStart at 0x5fb0 seeds the global USB frame counter at engine +0xb970 to current USB frame +100. queueInIrp at 0x6640 preincrements it. It posts 64 input IRPs, each eight microframes, at T+101 through T+164.
readHandler at 0x7a80 reads accepted actual counts, selects one of 128 free output IRPs, requeues the completed input (advancing the global counter), then submits output using that current counter. Ordered input originally T+101 therefore produces requeued IN and OUT at T+165. The USB output queue horizon is 64 USB milliseconds relative to that input request.
An IRP is 0xf0 bytes. Frame list begins +0x40; each 16-byte record has status +0, requested count +4, actual count +6, timestamp +8. Saved ring sample position is +0xd8, saved USB frame +0xe0, busy flag +0xe8.
IMPORTANT CORRECTION: This proves a 64-ms USB queue horizon, NOT 64-ms guitar signal latency in NI's original driver. Sample-position-addressed writes to the shared pending ring distinguish the two. We have not run the Intel kernel driver on this ARM Mac or measured original physical round-trip latency. Earlier statements conflating queue horizon and original signal latency were incorrect and must not guide the port.

3. Capture is serviced from the host input path as well as callbacks — established
readFrameList at 0x6f60 scans 64 input slots x eight microframes in order. It stops at pending marker 0x6c6c6974 ('llit', kUSBLowLatencyIsochTransferKey). It accepts success and 0xe00002e7 frame statuses.
convertInputSamples at 0x6e90 calls readFrameList directly before converting host input. Thus capture processing is not limited to waiting for the asynchronous completion callback.
readHandler at 0x7a80 also calls readFrameList. Slot 63's callback ends the original priming phase, resets input slot/microframe cursors and calls readFrameList again. During priming, normal sample conversion/output writes are declined.
Private exports: 00006f60_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__readFrameList.c; 00006e90_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__convertInputSamples.c; 00007a80_de_caiaq_driver_NIUSBAudioEngine__readHandler.c.

4. Clock and sample positions — established
writeHandler at 0x7ec0 copies the completed output IRP's stored ring sample position to engine current sample position +0xba0c. getCurrentSampleFrame at 0x68c0 returns it.
takeSimpleTimeStamp at 0x8100 uses the IRP saved USB frame and fractional byte position, computes time and rejects backwards updates. Timestamp-established flag +0xb98c; last accepted time +0xb980.
generateTimeStamp at 0xb790 uses anchor USB frame +0xbd70, anchor absolute host time +0xbd78, and smoothed nanoseconds-per-USB-frame interval scaled by 10000 at +0xbd58, plus byte-position fraction. It applies the recovered extra one-frame interval.
updateWallTimePerUSBCycle at 0xb880 samples USB frame before and after uptime until the frame is the same, then estimates interval and smooths equivalently to (new + old*1023 + 512) >> 10. Previous frame/time fields +0xbd80/+0xbd88.
getAnchorFrameAndTimeStamp at 0xba80 waits at most roughly 1.1 ms for a USB frame boundary.
timestampTimerCallback at 0xbbb0 refreshes interval/anchor and rearms at 128 ms. It is clock maintenance. No high-frequency OUT-submission polling loop was found there; do not invent one and attribute it to NI.

5. Current native differences — source facts
Driver/Audio/RK3AudioDriver.c ignores the host IO-cycle sample positions and moves samples through capture/render FIFOs. NativeAudioISO.c consumes render FIFO PCM, packs a separate per-transfer output buffer and submits a snapshot. It does not let the host place future samples into the queued output backing ring by target sample position.
With a 64-ms queue calendar, this turns the queue horizon into signal residence delay in OUR implementation. Build 4 kept the 64 input queue but moved OUT to received_frame+4, with pcm_ready gating, a capture freshness trim and callback-order guard. Strict/sanitizer/factory tests pass, but real hardware repeatedly rejects an isochronous request as too old. That is not a faithful solution to the original dataflow mismatch.
The current reference AudioSchedule.c remains an NI-derived pure scheduler; it does not by itself supply the original memory ownership, host write timing or direct capture-poll behavior. Matching its constants is insufficient to establish a faithful port.

6. Current API evidence and compatibility questions — unresolved
Local primary SDK: /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/IOKit.framework/Versions/A/Headers/usb/IOUSBLib.h (also the selected Xcode SDK).
Low-latency frame-list status/counts are updated at primary interrupt time and may be inspected before the completion callback. Completion callbacks can run several milliseconds later, with variable delay from higher-priority work. This matches why a four-ms callback-driven OUT calendar can miss deadlines.
The current API describes buffer reuse after completion. That is NOT sufficient evidence by itself that changing an outstanding output buffer is supported. The original kernel driver uses IOMemoryDescriptor/ring ownership; current user-space IOUSBLib mapping/bounce/snapshot behavior must be verified rather than assumed identical.
Unresolved questions: whether pending LL output maps live memory or snapshots/bounces it; when kernel/controller fetch output; concurrency and DMA visibility guarantees; safe ring-wrap descriptor equivalents; how host target sample frames align with device sample positions; how capture primary updates can be read without racing callback reuse/retirement; worker scheduling/QoS effects. A literal copy of old kernel pointer arithmetic into user space would not resolve these API contracts.

7. Required parity account BEFORE another implementation
Map each original method and data structure above to its ARM counterpart. Recover the complete output byte-placement/check-byte/ring-wrap formula, not only a successful initial sample vector. Trace host firstSampleFrame through the actual queued memory seen by USB. Match input polling, priming, current sample frame and clock-anchor relationships. Record exact API substitutions and evidence. If current user-space bindings cannot support a required ownership model, document the concrete limitation and evaluate the minimum compatible binding, rather than silently invent a different queue algorithm.
Do not blindly late-write outstanding buffers without a supported/validated ownership contract. Do not blindly change four to eight/sixteen ms. A new primary-frame polling service or alternate host buffering is only an unselected research possibility and is NOT approved as the lift-and-shift implementation. Audio-engine-contained panic recovery, however, is original NI evidence rather than inherently a new idea; see section 9 below. The exact current-platform mapping still requires proof. Diagnostic counters are verification aids, not a substitute design.

8. Validation needed after the faithful port is specified
The existing fixed-clock mock does not model deadlines. Add an advancing-bus reproduction of the actual too-old failure. Use uniquely identified ramp/impulse samples and host target times to test continuity, placement, ring wrap, deferred DMA visibility and jittered callback order. Test 128-frame host bursts versus 48-frame USB milliseconds, startup, capture freshness, missing/duplicate data, stop/cancel and recovery. Bounds/sanitizers/lifetime tests remain necessary but cannot substitute for temporal correctness. Then run actual silent transport, sustained guitar, all eight switches, pedal and host feedback, measuring generation stability and latency. No further development or hardware experiment was performed during the requested Beads capture.

9. Original audio-engine panic recovery versus full USB reconnection — review addition
readMicroframe at 0x8670 increments USBstreamingErrors on sync/device errors and, when correction is enabled, sets restart and arms the panic timer immediately. Lack of a free output slot and IsoTooOld submission failures schedule restart after 100 ms. panicTimerCallback at 0x5950 invokes the engine stop/start virtual slots, then clears restart. performAudioEngineStop at 0x6800 clears running state, disables/cancels panic/timestamp/statistic timers and aborts both AUDIO pipes. Later tearDown 0x5e30 / completeMemory 0x5f20 handle release. Device willTerminate/didTerminate are separate stages that remove user clients, deactivate the engine and close the USB interface/device.
This is evidence that NI has an audio-engine-level recovery path distinct from whole-device removal. The native implementation currently promotes an ISO error to full shared-USB failure/reconnection, which can interrupt controller EP1 availability. That is another fidelity difference to map explicitly. Do not describe audio-contained recovery as necessarily a novel architecture, and do not assume the stop/start wrapper call chain is fully ported merely from this observation. Reconstruct the complete original lifetime and restart semantics before changing it.
Source: ReverseEngineering/AudioDriver.md, priming/error-recovery section and stopping/power section, corroborated by the original method exports. Review by the read-only audio reconstruction agent identified this missing detail; no code was changed.

Resumed source review corrected several exact details: panic virtual calls resolve to IOAudioEngine pause/resume wrappers (vtable relocations 0x11640/0x11648), not direct start/stop. Only queueInIrp explicitly schedules IsoTooOld panic at 100 ms; queueOutIrp logs TooOld/TooNew and leaves its slot busy, with exhaustion later scheduling panic. performFormatChange sets input latency 4*(floor(rate/8000)+11), output latency and sampleOffset 8*(floor(rate/8000)+11): at48k 68/136/136 frames. Original host framework splits wrapped conversion/clip calls tail then head. Current public IOUSBHost optimized memory documents non-bounced kernel-backed storage and per-transaction Wrap; original shared-ring binding is therefore representable without FIFO snapshots. Current IOUSBLib user-side disassembly also has no payload copy; a user-space snapshot is not inherent to the API. Research remains explicit about DMA fetch/publication timing and actual validation.

RESUMED FAITHFUL PORT — implementation checkpoint, 2026-10-25
The user explicitly resumed after the documentation checkpoint and directed preserving original ring, timing and recovery, with only necessary ARM support changes. Original 64-request input-led calendar is restored; the 4 ms override is removed. A new portable AudioRing module matches exact NI mode-2/G1 wire mapping, check lanes, two-byte carry, original tail-before-head wrap conversion, priming and inactive clear footprint. It operates on externally supplied live storage rather than FIFO snapshots. Strict and sanitizer unit tests plus independent review pass.

Current platform binding evidence and source
Apple current IOUSBHostObject optimized allocation explicitly creates/maps controller-compatible IOBufferMemoryDescriptor storage without DMA bouncing. IOUSBHostIsochronousTransaction provides offsets and Wrap, including a microframe crossing a ring boundary. NativeHostUSB.h/.m implements that binding within the existing SINGLE interface owner; the closed legacy parent-device handle remains only for configuration/descriptor discovery. No second child-interface claimant is introduced. The mapped ring allocation and transaction metadata are retained through callback delivery. KernelUserShared transaction lists require the documented macOS26.4+ API for proven primary-update support in this personal current-Mac build. Build 3: "controls still respond. the sound is very soft. I almost had to go to max on the headphone volume output to hear anything. there's noticeable delay".

Build 4 implementation being diagnosed
Commit cc1afd9; installed 0.1.3 build 4, backup session /Library/Application Support/RigKontrol3/NativeDriverBackups/20261024T225037Z-08832e7b. Both installed signed ARM64 bundles matched all 12 manifest file hashes. The native adapter overrides output calendar to received_input_frame + 4 while preserving the recovered 64 input requests. AudioTiming.h advertises 48 input / 192 output sample frames; HAL stream latency is zero, safety offset 128. A pcm_ready gate blocks clock/PCM through priming and until some post-priming capture exists. Consumer-owned capture trimming retains request + 48 frames. Reversed input callback order fails before output encoding. These are source facts; four milliseconds is not an NI constant, measured round trip or validated reliable setting.

Listening run and its limited meaning
Tools/rk3-audio-client --monitor --gain 1 --buffer-frames 128 --live, PID 51327, printed actual 128-frame buffer, gain 1.000 and clamp 0.950. Final log:
80715 callbacks; 10331520 input frames; RMS 0.010865; input peak 0.223881; stop 0.
Earlier running snapshots were 36042 callbacks / 4613376 frames and 79548 / 10182144. The final input peak was below the output clamp, so this does not suggest the clamp caused crackling. Input peak does not measure output level. Frames represent approximately 215.24 seconds of delivered input at 48 kHz, not guaranteed continuous error-free wall time.
MIDI v4 run: CC4 count 54, range 0..127, last 127; CC80 and CC81 each count 4, CC82 count 2, switch last values 0. This log is not full eight-switch coverage and is not proof of reliable delivery while USB is restarting. The earlier full controller-only test is recorded in .2.

Actual silent reproduction — a sharper failure signal
After stopping the audible test, root sampled the installed ninf property at about 100 ms and ran a 15-second ordinary CoreAudio client with SILENT output at verified 128 frames. Guitar, effects, mappings and monitor gain are not required to reproduce the transport failure.
The silent client ended with 5552 callbacks, 710656 frames, RMS 0.002916, peak 0.011254 and stop 0. Despite exit 0, the concurrent status watcher recorded generation 99->105 and repeated flags 4 (failed) with error -536870162 / 0xe00002ee. Flags 1 are connected; 3 are connected+audio-running. After stopping audio, status settled at connected generation 105.
The current SDK IOReturn.h defines kIOReturnIsoTooOld = iokit_common_err(0x2ee), "isochronous I/O request for distant past". This establishes a real missed scheduling deadline, not merely a theory about FIFO sound quality.
NativeUSB increments generation on a successful new connection and reconnects after ISO engine errors. Therefore audio errors repeatedly reset the shared transport. This gives a concrete mechanism for intermittent controls; individual failed physical presses were not timestamp-correlated to each restart, so do not claim every missing control event has been proven separately.
The exact first failing submission is not yet identified. Four-millisecond output is the leading candidate, but an exceptionally delayed input requeue can return the same code. Stage/requested/current-frame/callback-lag context has not been captured. Do not turn that inference into a proved output-only diagnosis.

Why the tests missed the hardware failure
The fake USB writer records requested frame numbers but uses a fixed bus-frame stub and does not reject requests that are already late on an advancing bus. Its four-ms assertion proves the requested calendar, not that real macOS callbacks meet it. Constant-amplitude PCM checks are weak at detecting dropped/duplicated samples. Normal/sanitizer/factory/installer gates exercise important bounds, lifecycle, ownership, signature and ABI properties; none is an uninterrupted-audio acceptance test.
The ordinary audio helper returns success if stop succeeds and some callbacks/frames occurred. It does not detect restarts, inserted silence, underruns, sample continuity, audible distortion or round-trip latency. The MIDI helper similarly requires inspecting per-CC coverage and physical observations, not just exit 0. These limitations must be reflected in the next validation harness.

Additional known implementation departures and unverified secondary mechanisms
HAL io() ignores AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo target sample positions and exchanges samples through FIFOs. This differs from original NI's sample-addressed shared ring (.6).
pcm_ready waits for some capture, not a whole 128-frame block plus reserve. Capture shortages are zero-filled. The capture producer ignores short queue_write; render preparation ignores a short queue_read and inserts zeros. There are no counters for these missing/dropped frames.
Capture freshness trimming intentionally discards samples if occupancy exceeds request+48 (176 at a 128-frame request). This is not lossless recording and can introduce a waveform discontinuity. No evidence yet separates such secondary discontinuities from the already proved transport failures.
USB usually produces 48-frame increments per millisecond; a 128-frame host quantum spans 2 2/3 ms. Jitter/batching and reserves need deterministic continuity tests, rather than assuming queue capacity controls latency. Queue capacity is 16384 frames but active occupancy determines FIFO delay.
PERIOD 16384 is a zero-timestamp cadence/max-I/O constant, not a 16k audio batch. The SDK minimum is 10923; lowering it to 128 is not a valid latency fix.

Latest original-source discovery changes the repair direction
Original NI preposts output descriptors referencing the same wired ring that clipOutputSamples updates by host firstSampleFrame. The native version snapshots FIFO PCM at submission. Thus the previous 64 ms USB calendar became signal delay in OUR architecture; it does not prove the original NI driver had 64 ms audible latency. Reducing the calendar to four milliseconds attempted to compensate for a dataflow mismatch and failed on actual callback timing. The user now explicitly requires lift-and-shift fidelity. Do not blindly try 8/16 ms or invent another scheduling model. .6 must recover and map the original ownership/timestamp/ring contract first.

Present temporary helper: /private/tmp/rk3-status.c and /private/tmp/rk3-status. It enumerates the exact native audio UID and reads CFData ninf fields; it does not claim USB or start audio. The failed experiment used it for 25 seconds while the silent client ran 15 seconds. The helper is not committed.
Not implemented: durable per-call failure stage/context, callback lag distribution, capture-short/trim/overflow counters, render-underflow/overflow counters, queue occupancy range or end-to-end continuity assertions. These are potential verification aids for the faithful port, not permission to replace original behavior. title: Complete original MIDI/controller behavior and required client contracts
description: Native DIN parsing/packetization and the NI-derived fixed default controller mapper are implemented. Earlier installed physical tests verify all8switches, built-in pedal/calibration, local LEDs, incoming feedback and held-USB recovery. Full original parity is incomplete: sleep remains unverified; DIN/toe/external physical checks are separate; selectable pedal configuration, display/client-control surface and original NI user-client compatibility need explicit classification. NativeClient CFData is a new inter-bundle protocol, not an original NI IOKit selector-compatible service. Do not expand into an editor or shim project without .13 proving the required contract and minimum ARM binding.
acceptance_criteria: The NI original DIN/analog/digital component split and mapper provenance remain explicit. The original CC/toggle/calibration/feedback behavior is preserved through any necessary binding consolidation. All eight switches, built-in expression and incoming LED feedback work during sustained reliable audio, without phantom events, missed presses or shared transport churn. Reconnect/held-switch/sleep recovery is physically accepted. Toe/external axes and DIN remain explicitly limited until their dedicated physical tests pass. Earlier controller-only acceptance does not close combined-operation reliability.
notes:
Native DIN MIDI and separate Controller source/LED-feedback destination implemented and independently reviewed. Stateful MIDI parser, original NI controller CC profile/calibration, generation leases, activation/history race guards and async writes pass sanitizer tests. Bundle factory smoke passes. Installed MIDIServer Start, physical eight-switch/pedal/LED verification and calibration remain pending.
First installed source unavailable due AMFI rejection of ad-hoc MIDI signature, beforedriverStart. v0.1.1 Apple Development signed package verified locally; actual signed-host load/physicaltests await admin replacement.
Installed signed v0.1.2/build3 and verified cross-process CoreAudio CFData transport. CoreMIDI loads the native Controller source. Fresh calibration stored raw88..648 from555 samples. Persistent physical monitor recorded each of CC76..83 exactly twice, values0/127 and last0; built-in pedal CC4 reached0..127,55messages. User completed without reporting switch/LED faults. Initial apparent loss during earlier test coincided with45s client expiration/MIDIServer shutdown; live monitor now remains open. Incoming feedback CC80=127 physically lit LED1 (user confirmed); off check and audible audio pending.
Incoming Controller feedback CC80=0 also physically confirmed LED1 off. Persistent audio+MIDI clients now active together; further switch CCs and pedal CC4 continue during installed CoreAudio I/O.

DETAILED CONTROLLER/MIDI CHECKPOINT — 2026-10-25

Original component boundary
The NI 2.8.0 CoreMIDI plug-in carries existing DIN MIDI byte streams through the audio kext's user-client. It does NOT itself translate raw analog/digital pedal reports into CCs. The original audio dispatch has separate report paths: command 3 analog, command 4 digital and command 6 MIDI. The MIDI plug-in uses synchronous selector 3 (device info), synchronous selector 4 (MIDI output) and asynchronous selector 0 (MIDI input). Audio selector 12 injects host-produced MIDI but is not called by that plug-in. Exact profiles/calibration/LED policy were therefore separately reconstructed from NI Controller Editor/NIHardwareAgent evidence, not invented from port counts. See ReverseEngineering/MIDIDriver.md and ControllerMapping.md.

Current native arrangement, including a parity caveat
Driver/MIDI/RK3MIDIDriver.c implements MIDIDriverInterface2. It communicates with the single native audio/USB owner through versioned CFData CoreAudio properties. It has no old app, MainStage, socket or external bridge dependency. The actual hardware reply established one DIN input and one DIN output, which are separate unidirectional entities under a hardware device. A separate native Controller source and LED Feedback destination expose reconstructed NI controller policy. Moving that policy into the MIDI component is a structural consolidation compared with the original NI process split; it must be acknowledged and justified as a minimal platform substitution under .5, not described as a verbatim port of the original MIDI binary.
The current native owner handles the first RK3 only. Multiunit/serial-based identity is not implemented. UID org.rigkontrol3.ni-arm.usb.17cc1940; Controller identity appends .controller under key org.rigkontrol3.ni-arm.midi.identity. Stable endpoint identities are in a new namespace rather than the retired bridge's endpoints.

NI-derived profile implemented
Channel 1. Built-in expression axis 2 -> CC4. External analog axes 0/1 -> CC16/17. Physical switches 1-4 use raw bits 4-7 -> CC80-83. Switches 5-8 use raw bits 0-3 -> CC76-79. Toe/raw bit 8 -> CC64, not physically verified. Main switches toggle 0/127 on presses; releases do not emit another toggle. LEDs follow local assignment values. Host channel-1 CC feedback can override the corresponding state/LED, below 64 off and 64 or above on. Feedback does not echo into Controller input or route to DIN. This does not create effect-state output in Guitar Rig or another host that does not send it.

Fresh calibration
The user swept the built-in pedal fully three times. The native calibration tool measured raw 88-648 from 555 samples and saved a new Controller-device Data property. No old app calibration was imported. Property org.rigkontrol3.ni-arm.calibration is exactly four little-endian uint32 values: version 1, axis 2, raw_min, raw_max. Range must be within 0-1023 with at least 103 span. The main MIDI discovery loop validates it and atomically publishes endpoints; I/O applies the NI-derived normalization/deadband. The measurement tool rejects reconnect/history loss, insufficient samples and insufficient travel. Earlier app endpoints 88-633 are historical and must not replace this measurement.

Physical tests actually passed
The first 45-second MIDI monitor expired partway through the user's sequence, recording only CC80 and CC81 twice. With no remaining MIDI client, MIDIServer exited. That test-lifetime failure explains the first observed interruption; it was resolved by --live without a driver change. It is separate from the later build-4 ISO failure.
The repeated persistent test asked for all eight switches twice plus two full pedal sweeps. User replied Finished and reported no faults. Each CC76-83 had count 2, min 0, max 127, last 0. CC4 had count 55, min 0, max 127, last 0. User then separately confirmed CC80=127 lit physical LED 1 and CC80=0 extinguished it without foot presses.
These establish the full main-switch mapping, built-in travel and physical incoming LED 1 feedback in that tested configuration. They do not establish eight-effect mappings, automatic host effect-state feedback, toe support, external input operation or physical DIN I/O.

Combined-run failure supersedes any reliability claim
The final build-4 audio test user verdict was: "Audio glitches remain (crackling, dropping in and out), controls intermittently work". Its MIDI log contains CC4 count 54, CC80/81 count 4 each, CC82 count 2; no CC76-79 or CC83 messages were recorded in that run, so it does not establish complete eight-switch coverage. It cannot replace the earlier complete eight-switch coverage, and the earlier pass cannot establish reliable controls while failing audio repeatedly resets USB.
The silent reproduction records shared generations 99->105 with kIOReturnIsoTooOld. Shared-owner reconnects explain a concrete mechanism for controls becoming unavailable, although individual physical presses were not time-correlated to each transition. Keep this issue in progress until the faithful combined audio path and recovery are actually accepted.

Implementation checks and limitations
Stateful DIN parsing expands running status, preserves complete channel/system messages, handles realtime/SysEx and resets on loss/generation changes; NI compatibility filtering is documented. Output is a bounded immediate queue, not future timestamp scheduling. Send success means accepted for delivery, not USB completion. Generation/lifecycle leases reject stale output. Main-thread discovery and MIDI I/O-run-loop state ownership, input activation barriers, Stop/Start races, feedback separation and calibration updates have strict and sanitizer tests. Actual factory loading and signed MIDIServer acceptance pass. External physical DIN, toe/external pedals, multiunit operation and public distribution remain unverified. Source read/write generation failure can mark MIDI offline; do not conceal shared audio failures by remapping effects.

Utilities and evidence
Tools/rk3-midi-monitor.c: --live, SIGUSR1 cumulative stats, SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful disposal. It selects the Controller by private identity. Cumulative summaries do not preserve event order/timing, and process exit success means some CCs arrived, not all eight worked.
Tools/rk3-midi-feedback.c: sends only to Controller feedback, never DIN.
Tools/rk3-calibrate.c: installed cross-process calibration with generation/history guards.
Logs under active worktree .build/native/test/: midi-acceptance.log and midi-v4-acceptance.log. Essential results are embedded here so ignored build output is not the sole record. A dedicated retained calibration log was not found; its successful measurements were returned through tool output.
Follow-ups: .7 toe/external axes; rigkontrol3-fyx physical DIN; .3/.6 faithful combined audio and recovery.

Original HardwareAgent consumes private device-info/spec, raw report subscription, configuration, LED and MIDI paths; current ninf/nrpt/ncmd is not that ABI. Determine minimum original client exposure under the selected binding before changing it; do not port Controller Editor GUI/profile application or invent a shim by default. Green: exact parser/ABI/error/lifetime vectors at real seam, applicable configuration/readback/feedback and host contracts covered, physical8-switch/two-sweep/incoming-LED test concurrent with final audio; DIN/.7 are separate physical gates. title: Port original NI audio behavior to ARM with verified platform bindings
description: Core audio rings, mode-2 packing, positioned capture/render, NI calendar and host integration are implemented in the current ARM reconstruction. Installed0.2.1/build6 is verified, but the primary port is incomplete: a227.593-second silent run still produced a late request; exact original clock-maintenance cadence, channel gain/direct monitoring and broader original rate support are missing or differ. acceptance_criteria: All audio rows in .13 are matched or explicitly accepted necessary substitutions; confirmed missing original features are resolved. Actual signed ARM components deliver sustained clean audio with original rate/clock/recovery behavior and combined controls. Current .11 timing failure and .10 lifecycle gap must be resolved. Do not close on mock/factory/callback counts or obsolete build4 claims.
notes:
Native ARM audio bundle and owner implemented/reviewed. Real 5s USB capture/output/clock/stop and actual AudioServerPlugIn host-table callbacks pass. First format48k stereo. Installed CoreAudio client acceptance and audible guitar test still pending admin install.
Installed driver discovered by system_profiler; real standard CoreAudio client delivered144896inputframes/283callbacks/RMS0.002870 in3s and stopped0. Audible guitar and sustained/latency acceptance remain pending.
User physically heard dry guitar through installed native driver with simultaneous MIDI controls, but reported verysoft level and noticeable delay. Diagnostic monitor was deliberately0.1gain, so level check must be repeated without that attenuation. Latency remediation tracked40h.3; audio acceptance remains open.

AUDIO/USB IMPLEMENTATION AND HARDWARE CHECKPOINT — 2026-10-25

Recovered hardware contract and observed unit
Attached device: VID 0x17cc, PID 0x1940, USB release 0x000d, location 0x00100000. Configuration 1; interface 0 alt 0 has bulk OUT 0x01 / IN 0x81; alt 1 adds ISO IN 0x82 / OUT 0x06. Advertised endpoint capacity 512, interval 1. Fresh info reply was:
01 0d 00 06 00 03 09 29 02 02 00 00 01 01 02
NI-derived decoding: 2 audio inputs, 2 outputs, wire mode 2, 1 DIN MIDI input and 1 DIN output. Firmware target/current release matched 0x000d; no firmware upload was demonstrated necessary or performed.

Recovered startup operations implemented and actually needed
NI initUSB reapplies the advertised configuration even on warm opens, opens non-seizing interface/alt 1, clears bulk IN and OUT stall/toggle at both ends, starts persistent EP1 IN, then requests command 1. Original ClearPipeStall(true) sites are 0x0d84 and 0x0d99. Three warm opens and callback-drained closes passed only after matching the both-end reset.
Original RK3 audio initialization: 05 00 40 40 00 00 00. Controller configuration is 33 bytes beginning 0f 02 and otherwise zero. Auto-report subscription is 0b 01 02 05. Command 04 obtains a digital baseline; a valid low-nine-bit snapshot prevents held switches from becoming phantom presses.
Audio stop bytes: 09 ff ff 88 00 01; the unit returns 09 00. The original stop caller ignores the return, so the native stop accepts the bounded 0/1 acknowledgement while requiring the real 48 kHz start acknowledgement 09 01. Start bytes: 09 01 02 88 00 01.
Synchronous EP1 output bursts stalled when IN could not rearm. Bounded WritePipeAsyncTO plus pumping the same serial CFRunLoop preserved continuous input and fixed full startup. Stable write storage and pending-OUT cancellation/drain are part of ownership, not optional timing delays.

Current-host compatibility observations
SetPipePolicy rejected the original requested 136-byte capacity and even 512 on this host. Original calls ignore this result. The native adapter validates the actual ISO endpoint direction/type/number/capacity/interval and keeps descriptor bandwidth; command 9 still requests 136. This observed API substitution is documented, unlike an invented audio queue algorithm.
The current output API rejected trailing empty microframes with an exact-length buffer descriptor. Trimming only empty tail transactions fixed the observed invalid request-count/offset failure. Interior gaps, payload, calendar and check bytes remain. An all-empty output plan releases its slot without USB submission or clock advancement. Regression tests exercise this API geometry.

Original behavior versus current port
Driver/AudioCodec.c and AudioSchedule.c preserve independently recovered protocol/codec/reference scheduling vectors. The current NativeAudioISO implementation, however, snapshots FIFO PCM into per-transfer output buffers at submission, while NI writes directly to shared wired ring storage by host sample position. The HAL ignores I/O cycle sample times. This is a known fidelity defect, not a completed faithful ARM translation. See .6 for original methods, field offsets and clock/capture relationships. The 4 ms calendar at cc1afd9 is an unsuccessful attempt to compensate for the architectural difference.

Implementation topology and lifetime work already verified
One NativeUSB worker owns USB and services EP1 and audio together. CoreMIDI uses generation-leased public CoreAudio properties, not a second USB claimant. The engine uses wired LL ISO buffers, 64 IN slots and up to 128 OUT slots. Float capture/render queues are bounded and real-time functions avoid allocation, waits and USB calls. Pending callbacks retain storage; stopped/retired engines are unpublished, drained and reclaimed only after pending I/O and active calls cease. Retired-engine count is bounded. Generation checking rejects stale MIDI/LED work. The STOPPING state still reports USB connected while audio-running is false, preventing a normal audio stop from falsely taking controller transport away. These invariants have tests but do not repair the ring/timing mismatch.

Real pre-install transport tests, with limited claims
A five-second production native owner test captured 240006 frames, clock 68..240074, peak about 0.011101 and RMS 0.002067, stop 0 and drained close. Output was silence. A real audio CFPlugIn loaded into a diagnostic host passed Initialize/StartIO/GetZeroTimeStamp/DoIO/StopIO: 145 cycles, zero timestamp 0..32768, RMS 0.005260, I/O 0 and stop 0. Both actual bundle factories passed COM smoke. These establish real USB capture/completion and ABI operation; they never established clean guitar playback, low latency, DIN loopback or end-to-end timing fidelity.

Installed version chronology and sound verdicts
Initial installed audio 0.1.0 worked through an ordinary CoreAudio client: 3 seconds, 283 callbacks, 144896 input frames, RMS 0.002870, stop 0. Signed 0.1.2 later passed 5 seconds with calibration active: 469 callbacks, 240128 frames, RMS 0.002229, stop 0.
The 0.1.2 live dry monitor ran to 19431 callbacks / 9948672 input frames / RMS 0.007939 / stop 0. User heard guitar and controls worked, but sound was very soft and delay noticeable. The helper deliberately multiplied audio by 0.1, a 20 dB attenuation. This is a diagnostic-level confound, not proof of a hardware gain fault.
Installed 0.1.3 build 4 silent startup at verified 128 frames passed 3 seconds / 1162 callbacks / 148736 frames / RMS 0.002719 / peak 0.011175 / stop 0. The later unity-gain listening test FAILED subjectively and objectively; see .3. A successful short start or process exit does not override that result.

Formats and limits
Current native format is stereo, 48 kHz, Float32 host PCM and NI mode-2 wire format. The original advertises 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96 and 192 kHz; additional rates are not implemented/validated (rigkontrol3-7vl). Core/packet code supports additional recovered codec modes for tests, but that is not advertised hardware support. Physical round-trip latency has not been measured. A selected USB lead or HAL metadata is not a latency measurement.

Operational constraint
Do not run Tools/rk3-native-test or standalone audio-bundle Initialize/Start diagnostics while the installed CoreAudio owner has the RK3. They contend for the same interface and correctly return ExclusiveAccess; that is not a driver repair. Use a standard installed CoreAudio client and public control-property queries instead. rk3-driver-smoke now guards against an installed native device. No more tests or builds are to be run during the user's Beads-documentation pause.

AUDIT-COMPLETE BRANCH CARD — 2026-10-25
Gate: .13 records evidence; .17 must admit one minimum-change deployment/binding BEFORE this implementation or runtime path. This is planning only.
Rows A1-A12/B1-B16/F/audio identity/G. Aggregate audio port, not permission to explore. Next admissible work is the .17 deployment/binding decision. Then port only original rows through that binding; retain original serial-derived audio identity and inspect original firmware decision against attached release000d (original skip), without uploading firmware. Red: missing rates, cadence/gain/monitor/startup differences, changed identity/private behavior or failed .11 remain. Green: every applicable row satisfied with original-derived seam tests and signed installed acceptance, or specifically user-accepted exclusion. Final run: each advertised rate one600s silent standard-client run at128frames where supported;48k also three600s runs with MIDI active, zero unsolicited audio restarts/errors/generation changes; one120s unity guitar check with all8 switches twice, pedal two full sweeps and incoming alternating LED masks. Intentional reconnect is tested separately. Stop on first unexplained error or unknown original branch; file/update its card, do not tune queue/priority or flash firmware. Original hardware channels/firmware families outside attached RK3 are not silently added.

title: Reconstruct NI Rig Kontrol 3 drivers for native Apple Silicon
description: Faithfully port the original NI Rig Kontrol 3 audio/MIDI behavior and required capabilities to the attached Apple Silicon Mac, making only demonstrated ARM/current-macOS binding changes. The primary lift-and-shift is NOT complete. Current installed0.2.1/build6 matches the signed12-file package. Earlier0.2.0 physical guitar/eight-switch/expression/LED/held-USB tests passed; current0.2.1 still exhibits a measured late-request audio restart. Only48kHz is exposed; original rates and other capabilities/platform assumptions remain missing or unverified. Canonical next plan is rigkontrol3-40h.13: complete the original-to-ARM parity inventory and justify necessary platform substitutions before another implementation or diagnostic path. No new design, UI, workaround backend or guessed queue/priority change.
design:
GOVERNING PLAN — ORIGINAL NI RK3 LIFT-AND-SHIFT
User clarification, 2026-10-25: the primary objective is a lift-and-shift, not a replacement design. Before any new path, finish the necessary planning and capture it in Beads. This plan is the next gate. It does not authorize speculative tuning, a new backend, a new UI or further ad-hoc hardware experiments.

Definition of complete
Preserve the original RK3 driver behavior and externally needed capabilities on the attached Apple Silicon Mac. Recover behavior from the exact original binaries and instruction evidence, then change only what ARM and the current macOS interfaces demonstrably require. Original ring, packing, sample positions, clocks, queue calendar, error policies and recovery are the reference. Every necessary platform substitution must have a written reason and a test. A working prototype, decompiled functions, successful compilation or a few functional tests do not alone mean this objective is complete.

Current evidence boundary
The original audio 2.8.0 and MIDI 2.8.0 binaries were decompiled and cross-checked. Native ARM audio/MIDI components are built and installed. Version 0.2.0 passed subjective clear guitar at unity gain/128 frames, eight switches, expression range, local LEDs, incoming LED feedback and held-switch USB recovery. Version 0.2.1/build6 is now installed with all 12 files and signatures verified against manifest e2ee623f97af89c24d94e38d7061b460c3e1bd51dd13052d57b9937ecaa400e6. Its 120-second silent run passed, but its longer MIDI-active run failed after 227.593 seconds with TooOld. Thus stability and full timing parity remain incomplete. The ordering defect (.12) and audio-only recovery mapping (.8) are completed components; their closure does not close the primary objective.

Stage 1 — bounded parity inventory; the only next work
Use the existing original binaries, manifests, decompilation exports, assembly, SDK evidence and current source. Do not modify/install drivers, change scheduling, change queue lead, or start a new runtime experiment during this inventory.
Classify each sub-behavior and failure branch separately; matching command bytes must not conceal different readiness/failure policy. For each row record: original capability/method and image-relative address; evidence confidence; corresponding ARM code; status (matched, implemented/unverified, missing, or necessary substitution/unresolved); exact difference; current test/physical evidence; linked Beads issue; and completion/stop criteria.
Cover:
A. USB discovery/configuration, endpoint ownership, device information, initialization commands and conditional firmware-update behavior for this RK3.
B. Audio formats/rates/channels, conversion/check bytes, host-addressed rings, priming, descriptor ownership, IN/OUT calendars, latency/sample offset, timestamps, input polling and inactive-output clearing.
C. Kernel workloop/scheduling assumptions, panic delays, stop/drain, device removal, sleep/wake and original error classifications.
D. CoreMIDI DIN ABI, parser/packetization, port identity, send failures, client activation and delivery lifetime.
E. Raw controller reports, original mapper provenance, eight switches, expression calibration, toe/external inputs, assignments and incoming LED behavior.
F. Host/client-facing contracts. Distinguish ordinary CoreAudio/CoreMIDI compatibility from the original NI private user-client/control interfaces. Record what is required for the user's Guitar Rig/VST use and what is not yet demonstrated. Do not assume generic MIDI access proves every original NI-client interaction; do not start an NI compatibility layer or editor project merely because a private interface exists.
G. Installation, signing, rollback and limitations.
This is an audit of the attached RK3's original capability surface, not a port of unrelated NI device families or a new feature wish list.

Stage 2 — justify the architecture/platform substitutions
Before more timing work, account for the existing kernel IOAudioEngine/IOUSBPipe -> AudioServerPlugIn/IOUSBHost user-process substitution. Establish from current ARM/macOS availability and original dependencies which changes are unavoidable and which are our choices. Resolve the lowest-change supported binding using a bounded, read-only feasibility check; do not open a new implementation branch/backend/security change as part of the check. Record any signing, entitlement or security requirement before considering that route. The feasibility check is one bounded read-only evidence pass over pinned original dependencies, current local ARM/macOS artifacts/SDK and directly relevant official platform documentation. It must not install/download a new toolchain, request entitlements, load a driver, change security or start implementation. Stop when these sources cannot answer a required question; record the exact missing evidence/access and a narrow follow-up card rather than extending the search. Header presence/absence alone is not a complete feasibility proof. The output must be a written Architecture Necessity Decision in Beads before selecting another runtime measurement or implementation path; incompatibility with our chosen user process is not proof that choosing that process was unavoidable.
Known unresolved assumptions include modern primary-interrupt publication timing, last-output-client activity equivalence, sleep/wake behavior and the scheduling-domain change from the original kernel workloop. Shared KernelUserShared allocation does not prove exact primary cadence. A 54.5 ms handoff interval does not alone prove that changing QoS is the answer.

Stage 3 — implement only identified original parity gaps
Create or refine a child issue for each missing original behavior. For example, the ARM driver currently exposes only stereo 48 kHz, while NI advertised 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96 and 192 kHz; restoring those is original parity, not a new audio feature. Preserve all applicable original protocol values and transformations.
Complete confirmed missing original behavior with the minimum justified ARM/macOS adapter. Do not substitute a new queue algorithm, guessed delay, UI, generic bridge or speculative recovery policy. If an original capability is deliberately excluded, the primary objective cannot be called full parity without the user's explicit acceptance of that narrower scope.

Stage 4 — validate/fix necessary bindings using one bounded path at a time
The late-request fault (.11) is a timing-parity blocker, not an invitation to general performance optimization. Before its next action, write a branch card containing:
1. The exact original behavior/parity row being preserved.
2. The observed failure and evidence, with facts separated from inference.
3. One falsifiable hypothesis and the reason it is the next highest-value one.
4. One minimal measurement or correction and its scope/cost.
5. The red/green command, exact duration/repetition count, error predicate, success threshold and stop/escalation condition;120 seconds already passed before a227.593-second failure, so the word sustained alone is insufficient.
6. Why this is necessary for ARM/current macOS rather than a new design.
Current measured fault: NI requeue target remains exactly old frame+64; observed completion-to-enqueue entry was about 65.94 ms, with a 54.54 ms raw-handler-to-worker interval and 17.70 ms elapsed enqueue call. Ordered hold was negligible and no FIFO backlog was present. This localizes the miss but does not distinguish worker CPU work, blocking, descheduling or publication delay.
Candidate next measurements are not approved decisions yet: a narrowly scoped stack/scheduler capture, or bounded self-CPU/phase observations if access is unavailable. Select ONE only after Stages 1–2 and record its gate. Do not run parallel speculative sampling/QoS/backend branches. No numeric priority, private interrupt flag or queue-lead tuning without evidence. Stop a branch if it cannot distinguish the hypothesis, changes unrelated behavior, or requires a broader architecture/security decision; record that result instead of extending the rabbit hole.

Stage 5 — original-capability acceptance and cleanup
Automated tests must compare original-derived vectors, actual callback ownership/order, clocks and failure policies at the real seam. Installed acceptance must cover sustained clear audio with all eight switches, expression and LED feedback; every restored original format/rate; reconnect, Stop/Start, sleep/wake and inactive-output behavior. DIN/toe/external inputs need the appropriate physical setup; record unavailable hardware as unvalidated rather than inventing success.
Remove temporary DEBUG timing instrumentation after causal verification. Run final signed package, rollback, strict and sanitizer gates, then installed acceptance on the clean build. Commit/push code and export/sync Beads. Close the parent only when the matrix is satisfied or the user has explicitly accepted documented exceptions.

Branch admission rule
Every subsequent path must already have its original-parity justification, bounded plan, evidence, test, stop criterion and Beads link before execution. This task produces the matrix and necessary-binding decision; it is not complete merely because this plan has been written.
